subject: Literature
title: Climate Fiction and the Dystopian Future
description: Learn Climate Fiction and the Dystopian Future in one minute.

hook.text: Climate fiction, or 'cli-fi,' is the fastest-growing subgenre of dystopian literature in the twenty-first century.

buildup.text: Writers like Kim Stanley Robinson, Jeff VanderMeer, and Richard Powers use fiction to make climate science visceral.

discovery.text: Studies show that cli-fi novels change readers' attitudes toward climate change more effectively than scientific reports.

twist.text: Some cli-fi authors struggle with the genre because real climate news already reads like dystopian fiction.

climax.text: Climate fiction may be dystopian literature's most urgent evolution, turning data into stories people actually feel.

punchline.text: When science fails to move people, stories step in.

quiz.question: What do studies show about climate fiction's impact on readers?
options: It has no measurable effect on attitudes
It changes readers' attitudes toward climate change more than scientific reports
It only appeals to readers who already believe in climate change
